text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when the nerve stimulus is removed: the motor neuron stops releasing acetylcholine, so the fibre is no longer excited, and SERCA pumps calcium back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Calcium then falls, tropomyosin re-blocks the myosin-binding sites on actin, and a stronger stimulus would cause sustained contraction rather than relaxation. The question is cut off after "when:", so this assumes the standard textbook answer.

CONFIDENCE: 88
